combats.encounter: Vine-and-mud creature at the river crossing
combats.note: The DM runs the fight without an initiative roll or encounter tracker. Vola’s participation is confirmed afterwards, but her individual actions are not recorded.

openingActions.summary: Scratches the summoning-circle runes with his shadow sword; the mists begin blowing away. He stops scratching when attacked.
Erupts from the river and slams Delwath for 10 bludgeoning damage.
His cold armor effect deals 10 cold damage to the creature that struck him.
Fights alongside the party. The DM later explicitly corrects her omission from the narrated turns; no particular attack or result is supplied.
openingActions.note: The in-segment action prompt omitted Vola; the later correction establishes participation across the encounter without assigning her an initiative slot.

entries.summary: Curses the creature, then attacks with Booming Blade and misses.
At Wellby’s suggestion, overturns the earth where Delwath had scratched the circle, destroying that portion of the runes. The whole circle is not yet erased.
Stays still about 15 feet away, takes careful aim, and hits with an arrow. Sneak attack applies because Delwath is in melee; the DM appears to accept 17 damage.
entries.note: The accepted numerical utterance is transcribed as “1717”; the hit is clear.

entries.summary: Charges in and attacks with Shatterstorm using Booming Blade. The table resolves the normal hammer damage and explains that extra Booming Blade damage requires movement; Riswynn reports an eight on the digital die.
entries.note: The transcript does not clearly identify whether eight is the final damage total; it never separately resolves the later movement-triggered damage.

entries.summary: Uses Inner Power for two ki, with 3d10 force damage rolled. The creature fails its save, is knocked backward and prone. Kenzo rushes forward and lands one bonus-action unarmed strike with advantage against it.
entries.note: Neither the saving-throw ability nor a final damage total is spoken. Sleep is a rejected joke, not a cast spell.

entries.summary: Stands and steps among Kenzo, Riswynn, and Delwath, releasing spores. Constitution saves let Delwath and Riswynn shake off the effect; Kenzo is poisoned and hears howling and barking. Wellby is outside the effect. Slam attacks of 12 at Delwath and 6 at Riswynn both miss.
Casts Hex, choosing Wisdom for its disadvantage, then hits with his sword for an accepted 13 damage including the Hex contribution. Several vines blacken and crumble.
Again stays still, takes aim and hits with an arrow at the blackened part of the creature.
entries.note: The DM’s numerical utterance is transcribed as “914”; no unambiguous damage total is recoverable.

entries.summary: Touches the creature and hits with Inflict Wounds. Its body blackens and dehydrates; it staggers visibly hurt.
Casts Vicious Mockery with glowing hedge-clipper imagery. The creature fails its Wisdom save and has disadvantage on its next attack.

Hits with his quarterstaff and spends a ki on Flurry of Blows. All three attacks still hit after rerolling with disadvantage from poison; the initially apparent critical hit is lost when the lower die is used.

Misses Kenzo with its first slam, made with Vicious Mockery disadvantage. Its second slam hits Delwath’s AC 17 for 9 bludgeoning damage without disadvantage. Another spore burst calls for Constitution saves; Kenzo remains poisoned but the effect does not worsen.
entries.note: The other targets’ second saving-throw results are not individually stated.

entries.summary: Hits again with his sword; the DM settles the spoken damage at 11. The creature dries out, loses an arm, and is nearly unable to hold itself together.
entries.note: The actor is inferred from the adjacent Delwath response and continuing sword/Hex sequence; the attack declaration is not clearly preserved.

entries.summary: Excavates the riverbank immediately behind the creature, creating a water-filled gap behind its feet.

Remains still, aims, and lands a critical shortbow hit. The DM declares it lethal without totaling the damage; the shot knocks the creature into the mud and river, where the renewed flood sweeps it away.
A pale gray-white stream returns from the dying creature to him, described as the curse returning.

ending.summary: The creature dies and is swept downstream. The obstruction breaks, water floods freely through the valley, and the mists clear.
